original_review_metadata.title: Label Detective
original_review_metadata.instruction: Choose one unfamiliar packaged food and practice your label-checking process.

original_review_metadata.title: Cross-Contact Spotter
original_review_metadata.instruction: Notice one possible cross-contact point in a real food situation.
original_review_metadata.safety_note: You never need to eat anything uncertain to complete this challenge.

steps: Look at how food is prepared, handled, or served.
Examples could include shared serving utensils, preparation areas, or cooking equipment.
Your job is only to notice and identify the question—not to prove that cross-contact occurred.

original_review_metadata.title: Build One Backup Plan
original_review_metadata.instruction: Pick one upcoming activity and make one simple backup plan.
original_review_metadata.safety_note: Using the backup counts as the plan working—not failing.
original_review_metadata.completion_message: You tried the skill. That counts. +15 XP
original_review_metadata.source_basis: Meyer & Naveh self-management framework; Celiac Disease Foundation
steps: Name your Plan A.
Choose one realistic Plan B: a snack, food from home, eating beforehand, another location, or another strategy that works for you.
Keep it simple enough that you would actually use it.

original_review_metadata.title: Make a 5-Minute Restaurant Plan
original_review_metadata.instruction: Choose one restaurant situation and see whether you can make a useful plan without researching forever.
original_review_metadata.safety_note: This challenge is about practicing focused planning, not proving that five minutes is always enough for every restaurant.

steps: Set a short planning window—about five minutes for this challenge.
Check the restaurant/menu and identify the one or two questions that matter most.
